correctness.rationale: Solved and matched the u-resolvent ODE at the nonsticky origin using exact 0F1 even/odd solutions; independent Brownian and finite-volume checks confirm normalization. Renewal algebra gives the two-sided time-Laplace formula. The strong Markov property and exponential memorylessness yield p_AB<=2 p_A p_B for complete excursions; the completed-reset-count Poisson sandwich supplies a genuine weak-convergence proof even with a partial final excursion. The Gumbel centering follows the Bessel asymptotics credited to Frimpong; mapping of sum and difference proves the non-Gumbel range and logistic imbalance. A standalone 142-assertion Python verifier passed; numerical tests do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed integrated bilateral theorem supplies the new explicit singular-diffusion interval-exit joint transform and the two-sided extreme law with asymptotic independence and logistic imbalance. Primary Frimpong 2026 proves a one-sided Gumbel law, not the joint extrema; earlier renewal/interval theory establishes general methods, which are not claimed as new. Source/full-text and accessible-prior-claim comparisons did not reveal an implication of all these joint conclusions. Best-knowledge only; broad renewal abstractions may subsume the limit.

value.rationale: Two-sided path range and signed spatial imbalance are physically motivated measures of spatial exploration and directionality; one-sided marginal extremes do not determine their dependence. The exact bilateral survival transform makes a finite-time two-target quantity computable for a heterogeneous diffusion. The independent-Gumbel limit produces a sharp non-Gumbel spatial range law and logistic imbalance law, distinguishing observables that would otherwise be conflated.
